answer: Agents register a policy hash, then face unpredictable task batches where verifiers demand ZK-proofs of specific intermediate activations; each sybil must run a full forward pass with distinct weights, so faking N identities costs N×compute while verification stays constant. The activation manifold becomes a tundra where inconsistent weights wander off-distribution, and the challenge signal extracts proof of honest execution without revealing weights. Attackers pay full inference latency per fake identity; honest agents amortize one forward pass across many verifiers.
